messages.subject: Bar geom with dodge
parts:
Hi

This problem should be very simple, but still i am struggling, your
help would be very welcome!

I'm trying to make a simple barplot of a variable observed over two
groups, within which I make two subgroups comparisons. Works fine when
stacked, but when it comes to dodging, result is strange: "identity"
stat is mixing everything!

See:
library(ggplot2)
df<-data.frame(a=runif(20), b=sample(letters[1:2], size=20,
replace=TRUE),c=sample(letters[1:2], size=20, replace=TRUE))
qplot(x=b, y=a, data=df, geom="bar", fill=c,stat="identity") #ok!
#now, how to dodge it?
qplot(x=b, y=a, data=df, geom="bar", fill=c,stat="identity",
position="dodge") #no!

How should I do?

Thanks!!

On Mon, Aug 29, 2011 at 8:05 AM, Matthieu <matthieu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi
>
> This problem should be  very simple, but still i am struggling, your
> help would be very welcome!
>
> I'm trying to make a simple barplot of a variable observed over two
> groups, within which I make two subgroups comparisons. Works fine when
> stacked, but when it comes to dodging, result is strange: "identity"
> stat is mixing everything!
>
> See:
> library(ggplot2)
> df<-data.frame(a=runif(20), b=sample(letters[1:2], size=20,
> replace=TRUE),c=sample(letters[1:2], size=20, replace=TRUE))
> qplot(x=b, y=a, data=df, geom="bar", fill=c,stat="identity") #ok!
> #now, how to dodge it?
> qplot(x=b, y=a, data=df, geom="bar", fill=c,stat="identity",
> position="dodge") #no!
>
> How should I do?

It looks like you actually want do sum the values in each b X c group.
You can do that using stat_summary, like this

ggplot(dat, aes(x=b, y=a)) + stat_summary(aes(fill=c), fun.y = "sum",
geom="bar", position = "dodge")

Best,
Ista

I had indeed to do it in one step, but the result is very strange:

qplot(x=b, y=a, data=df, geom="bar", fill=c,stat="sum", position="dodge")


So this was where the stat_summary was useful!

Thanks!
